falsifier: fewer claims than the corpus band (about 3.4 must-finds) rest on such a fact, or every such fact reduces to one predicate
hypothesis: after registry version 8, a material share of the corpus's reference claims rest on a fact the sources state and no predicate or graph field can hold
intervention: read all 331 reference claims of the 13 tuned cases (242 STRIDE, 89 ASVS) against each case's source, stated model attributes and signed facts, and classed the fact each claim rests on: structure 17, field 39, predicate 52, silent 222, none 1. Must-finds: silent 88, predicate 36, field 23, structure 6, none 0. The one fact no predicate holds: case 08's group membership and leavers reach the directory only through a nightly pull (08 stride 16 rests on it; 08 stride 19 and 08 asvs 2 rest on it in part). Three signed rows may understate their source: 04 'we have never expired one' (credential-expiry and credential-rotation read unknown), 04 'Redis has no password on it' (authentication-mechanism reads unknown), and 10 the admin reaching the database from anywhere with no jump host (no internet-exposure row)
reconsider_when: a new case enters the corpus, the registry versions, or a sitting re-reads a case
scope: tuned cases only, holdouts excluded; one agent's reading, not signed; it reads only facts some reference claim rests on, so a stated fact no claim uses is not counted; it says a predicate exists, not that the assert node writes it
signature: a reference claim rests on a stated fact no assertion predicate can hold

falsifier: more than half of the settled principal rows in the archive reach an element
hypothesis: most settled assertion rows about a principal reach no element, because a principal reaches one only through a stated represented-by row
intervention: re-resolved every archived assertion emission with today's code (90 artifacts, 204 case-runs, tuned cases, head-only sweeps skipped) and asked, through the STRIDE rules' own helpers _principals_of and _presented_on, whether each settled row about a principal or a credential reaches an element. Principals: 443 of 444 rows stranded (authorization-grant 308, mfa-requirement 64, credential-presented 60, administrative-authority 11); the one that reaches is a represented-by row itself; 34 distinct principals. Credentials: 116 of 161 reach, all through credential-presented on a flow. The Evidence Catalog still offers every stranded row to the lanes (offered()); what is lost is every reader that needs a place: the candidate rules and ground_places. Of the 34 principals, 16 share a word with exactly one element (about 14 of those correct on reading, two wrong: 'anything that can reach the service' and 'corporate laptop'), 7 with several, 11 with none
reconsider_when: a represented-by row can be settled without a source sentence, for example by an answer to an intake question (#1225)
scope: archived emissions, tuned cases, luna and other benchmark models mixed; repeated runs count each time; the name-match figures are one agent's reading and are not a proposed rule
signature: a fact about a principal or a credential reaches no graph element

falsifier: the links place fewer than half of the stranded rows, or need more than about three questions a report
hypothesis: asking the submitter which element each principal is (a #1225 link question) places most stranded principal rows and gives the rules leads they cannot reach today, at a small question count per report
intervention: re-resolved the archived assertion emissions (tuned cases, head-only sweeps skipped), added a stated represented-by row for each principal from one agent's reading of which element it is (seven principals answered 'none of these'), and re-ran STRIDE candidate generation with and without the links. 167 case-runs carry a principal; they would ask 2.2 link questions on average, 5 at most, after folding spelling variants. The links place 351 of 443 stranded rows (authorization-grant 227, mfa-requirement 64, credential-presented 60). New leads: spoofing-second-factor-stated-absent 62 (all case 01, shopper accounts to entity:shopper), spoofing-standing-credential 13. The only new leads at a sweep B missed must-find are the 62 at case 01 ref 0, where the lane already drafts at the place and loses the claim by verb, so the corpus recall ceiling is about zero
reconsider_when: #1225 is built, or a corpus case carries an answers Source
scope: archived emissions, tuned cases, answers from one agent's reading rather than a submitter; authorization-grant rows have no rule, so placing them serves only the place readers; sweep B misses are one run
signature: a fact about a principal or a credential reaches no graph element

falsifier: an early ranking at the same question count settles at least 80% of what the report-ranked questions settle on the same pool
hypothesis: questions chosen right after extraction, before analysis, settle nearly as many needs-info findings as questions ranked from the finished report
intervention: on sweep B stage 1's 13 tuned cases (175 needs-info findings), counted the findings whose every related unknown a question set answers. Report-ranked, any open fact, 6 a case: 78 questions settle 129. Report-ranked, model attributes only: 76 settle 69. Early, the three most-cited attributes (authentication, encryption_in_transit, encryption_at_rest) ranked by how many STRIDE candidates name the element, 6 a case: 78 settle 46; uncapped: 184 settle 88. Early, by leads over all attributes: 78 settle 25. #1225's first rule: 122 settle 62. The findings cite 170 element attributes and 79 free-text subjects; the lanes raise the subjects, so no early question can ask them
reconsider_when: a job can pause after extraction, so a paid pair can measure what early answers change in the lanes

falsifier: the draft-based list settles fewer findings than a verdict-based list taken from another critic sample of the same drafts

intervention: two archived critic replays of Baseline 6bff717's drafts with the same critic prompt (evals/runs/20260925T-critic-corpus-1208/rulings and 20260925T-critic-cross-lane, prompt files unchanged between them), cases 01, 04 and 10, six greedy questions a case. Verdict-based lists from the two samples share 7 of 18 questions. Sample A's 32 needs-info findings: its own list settles 19, sample B's list 10, the draft-based list 17. Sample B's 36: own 15, sample A's 10, draft-based 11. So a verdict-based list keeps 20 of 34 (59%) of its value on another sample, and the draft-based list, identical for both, reaches 28 of 34 (82%). falsifier: the number of distinct types keeps growing with each case, or types read off the first cases cover less than 80% of the later cases' items
hypothesis: the critic's free-text questions, and the missing facts behind the claims that rest on silence, fall into a small set of question types that stops growing as cases are added, so a closed table of types parameterized by element can hold them
intervention: one agent read sweep B's 79 free-text questions on the 13 tuned cases and typed each; the 222 silent claims of QA-2026-09-26-03-E1 were typed by a keyword table over their missing-fact labels. Free text: 11 types (capacity 24, audit evidence 17, authorization scope 17, stored-copy integrity 5, reachability 5, provenance 3, physical access 2, code execution from content 2, stored-copy access 2, validation 1, destination 1), the last new one at case 09; types from the first 6 cases cover 40 of 46 later items, from the first 9 cases 24 of 24. Silent claims: 13 types, the last new one at case 12; types from the first 6 cases cover 128 of 130 later items; one label stayed untyped (token custody, which credential-custody holds). At the level of the specific question the set does not saturate: 77 distinct texts of 79, and 161 distinct missing facts growing by about 12 a case

scope: 13 tuned cases, STRIDE, one sweep, one agent's typing, keyword typing for the silent claims; the holdout cases are not read, so unseen input is approximated by leaving later cases out; a type question is less specific than the critic's text, which a table would trade for consistency
signature: the questions a report asks change when the critic is sampled again

falsifier: the free model answers the critic schema and names at least one open fact as a question kind
hypothesis: a free OpenRouter model can stand in for the deployed critic model when the question-kinds prompt is measured, at no cost
intervention: critic-replay of Baseline 6bff717's case 01 drafts with the question-kinds prompt (1ca916d2) on qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free and google/gemma-4-31b-it:free, six tries each over 30 minutes. Gemma returned a 429 from the upstream shared pool on every try. Qwen answered and passed the schema: 16 of 18 verdicts agree with the archived terra critic. It named 10 open facts, all as a free-text subject and none as a question kind: 9 subjects are only an attribute name (authentication, encryption_in_transit, encryption_at_rest), where the element_id and attribute fields exist for that fact, and 1 is 'rate or size limits', which the capacity-limits kind covers. None of the 93 subjects in the archived terra rulings is only an attribute name
reconsider_when: a free model is proposed for another critic measurement: a free model's fallback rate measures its instruction following as much as the table
scope: one case, one sample per model, STRIDE; qwen only, because gemma never answered; the deployed critic model is terra, so this says nothing about the table on terra
signature: the questions a report asks change when the critic is sampled again

falsifier: the free model names an open fact with no place in the model as a question kind, or its entries are free text by choice rather than by a broken emission
hypothesis: a free OpenRouter model can stand in for the deployed critic model when the question-kinds prompt is measured, at no cost
intervention: E9's Qwen replay read again, entry by entry. E9 counted 9 attribute-name subjects; that was a misreading. Each of the 9 facts appears twice in the same verdict: once as a sound element_id and attribute reference, and once with the same element_id and attribute plus subject set to the attribute's name and assertion set to '}],', which is schema punctuation inside a string. A schema-constrained decoder cannot write that, so the endpoint did not constrain the output to the schema. OpenRouter lists structured_outputs for this endpoint but not response_format, and its documentation says some endpoints treat a schema as a strong hint. Corrected figures: 9 facts with a place in the model, each sound, each with a broken duplicate; 1 fact without a place ('rate or size limits'), written as a subject where capacity-limits fits; 0 typed. Whether the model saw the kinds' descriptions is not known, because the forwarded request is not visible
reconsider_when: the critic prompt lists the kinds and the seam refuses a mixed entry: replay Qwen once more to read whether it types the facts that have no place in the model
scope: one case, one sample, STRIDE, qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free; the deployed critic model is terra, so this says nothing about the table on terra
signature: the questions a report asks change when the critic is sampled again

falsifier: the two samples' top-6 verdict-based question lists share no more than E7's 7 of 18 on cases 01, 04 and 10, or more than 20% of the facts with no place in the model fall back to a subject

All 13 cases: 53 of 78 shared; a list keeps 89 of 119 (75%); no-place facts 126 and 116, 83 in both. Citations: 261 typed, 15 free text, fallback 5% (3 cases: 45 and 3, 6%). Every entry used one spelling. The script is in QA-2026-09-26-03.md

falsifier: no ranking read from the System Model before analysis settles more than 50% of what the report ranking settles at 6 and at 10 questions a case, on both critic passes
hypothesis: with question kinds, a question list ranked before analysis from the System Model and STRIDE's candidates settles most of what the list after the report settles
intervention: E11's two terra passes, 13 tuned cases (170 and 167 needs-info findings). An early list ranks every (element, attribute) and (element, kind) pair by a prior read from the other 12 cases (citations per element of that type, leave one case out). Three rankings, the pick made on pass a and checked on pass b. Prior only: 41% and 44% of the report ranking at 6 a case. Prior times (1 + STRIDE candidates naming the element): 64% and 59% at 6, 63% and 62% at 10. The same plus a large boost where a candidate's fact names the attribute 'unknown': 62% and 75% at 3, but 50% and 56% at 6. Kinds are 261 of 577 citations and trust_zone 16, so an early list now reaches the facts E5 said only the critic raised. The script is in QA-2026-09-26-03.md

falsifier: the five runs with the signed answers find no more must-finds, and settle no more findings, than the five without them
hypothesis: a submitter's answers to a case's top questions, written in as a resumed job writes them, make the analysis find more must-finds and leave fewer findings conditional
intervention: the answered mode (#1272) on case 06, five runs each side on luna-pro. Pre-flight, no answers: /bin/bash.2281 for one run, against an estimate of /bin/bash.044 scaled from a computed sweep figure, so five and five cost about .28; 7 of 10 must-finds, 33 of 33 findings needs-info. A ballot of 18 questions (the report's top 10 and the early list's top 10) went to the maintainer, who left every answer blank: the source describes database operations and states no granted permission or enforcement, so an answer would invent owner knowledge. The upstream pytm model (OWASP Threat Model Cookbook, onlinegame.py) sets no security property on any element or flow either. The corpus's other cases are cookbook conversions or agent-written systems, so none has an owner who knows more than its source
reconsider_when: a system with an owner who can answer is available, or an ablation design is chosen: withhold statements from a case whose source states controls and answer from the withheld text
scope: one case, one pre-flight run; the no-answers run is kept as a sample for a later pair
signature: do a submitter's answers make the report more correct
